title: Pass or Fail: Running a Scenario and Judging Every Step of the Trace Against Written Criteria

questions.question: Why must a scenario run end in a verdict and not in a plot?
options: A plot cannot show overshoot
A verdict takes less space in the log
Plots cannot be made without a display
A run passed by looking at it has no test behind it: next month's slow worsening is not looked at, and the verdict names the step and the criterion that failed
questions.explanation: Someone looked today and it was fine. Nobody will look at every run, and a slow drift past the limit is caught only by a check that runs every time.

questions.question: Why is overshoot a fraction of the step's size?
options: A fraction is quicker to compute than a distance
So that it cannot be negative
So a big step and a small one can be compared, and the settling band, also a fraction of the step, means the same for both
Because the trace is stored as fractions
questions.explanation: An overshoot of 0.05 is serious on a step of 0.1 and trivial on a step of 1.5. As a fraction of the step, one limit serves both.

questions.question: An underdamped step up and its exact mirror down are measured. What should the numbers be?
options: Opposite: 0.0759 going up and -0.0759 going down
Different: a step down has no overshoot, since it ends below the target
Identical, the same overshoot 0.0759, rise 0.1800 and settling 0.5600: past the target means the side the step was going toward
Half as large going down, since gravity helps
questions.explanation: A step down that goes below its target has overshot. Measured as past the target in the direction of travel, the mirror image gives the same numbers.

questions.question: The target is changed to where the position already is. What should the analysis do?
options: Leave it out: it moves nothing, so there is no overshoot, rise or settling to report
Report a perfect step: no overshoot, no rise time, settled at once
Fail the run, since a target was set and nothing moved
Report a step with a settling time of -1
questions.explanation: Nothing moved, so there is nothing to measure. Reporting it as a perfect step would improve the averages with a step that never happened.

questions.question: A loop oscillates for ever around its target. What does its settling time read, and what does the verdict say?
options: The period of the oscillation, and the verdict passes
-1, which is not a time, and the verdict says settling: it never stayed within the band
Zero, since it is at the target on average
The length of the step, and the verdict says final error
questions.explanation: Settling means staying inside the band for the rest of the step. An oscillation leaves it again and again, so there is no settling time to give.

questions.question: The same scenario is run against a good sensor, one 60 ms late and one stuck from 1 s. What came out?
options: A pass, then failures on every step (overshoot, settling and final error), then failures on all but the overshoot of the last step, which did not move at all
Three passes: the scenario was the same
Three failures on the same criterion
A pass, a pass and a failure on the last step only
questions.explanation: The late sensor rings on every step. The stuck one leaves the position unmoved for the last step, so that step has no overshoot and still never settles.
